claims.claim: MCP's 2026-07-28 revision removes protocol-level sessions from the core (no initialize/notifications/initialized handshake, no Mcp-Session-Id header, per-request self-description via _meta)
MCP 2026-07-28 requires ttlMs/cacheScope on list-result endpoints (tools/list, resources/list, prompts/list) for cacheable, prompt-cache-friendly discovery
MCP Tasks moved from core to the io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks extension; polling (tasks/get, tasks/update) replaces blocking tasks/result; tasks/list removed
MCP's own spec states tool behavior descriptions/annotations are not inherently trusted; user consent and explicit authorization are implementation responsibilities
SSE stream resumability (Last-Event-ID) was removed from Streamable HTTP - a broken response stream now loses the in-flight request; clients must re-issue as a new request
A2A defines 4 primitives: Agent Card (discovery/capability JSON), Task (stateful unit of work), Message (role-tagged exchange), Artifact (task output)
A2A remote agents are explicitly documented as opaque black-box systems - internal workings, memory, tools not exposed across the client/agent boundary
A2A is governed by the Linux Foundation (donated by Google, June 2025), multi-vendor TSC (AWS, Cisco, Google, IBM, Microsoft, Salesforce, SAP, ServiceNow), 150+ supporting orgs, Apache-2.0
A2A transport is HTTP(S) + JSON-RPC 2.0, with SSE streaming and server-initiated push notifications to a client webhook for long-running/disconnected tasks
OpenAI Agents SDK keeps a small primitive core (Agents, agents-as-tools/handoffs, guardrails) and layers sessions, tracing, MCP, sandbox execution around it
OpenAI Agents SDK Session interface has one local implementation (MemorySession) and one cloud implementation (OpenAIConversationsSession) behind the same interface
Sandbox agents (workspace/session/snapshot surfaces) are a beta feature of the OpenAI Agents SDK Python docs
Microsoft Agent Framework distinguishes Agent (open-ended), Harness (long multi-step work), and Workflow (graph-based, type-safe routing, checkpointing, HITL) as three layers
Microsoft Agent Framework is the direct successor to AutoGen and Semantic Kernel
claims.note: 3-way independent convergence - the single most-corroborated claim in this whole corpus by source count.

claims.claim: Microsoft Agent Framework checkpointing is SDK-provided via pluggable storage; CosmosCheckpointStorage is the one confirmed reference implementation, and it is cloud-backed

PydanticAI's durable-execution capability is an attachable capability over Temporal/DBOS/Prefect; the three backends do not behave identically for mid-execution backend swap (Temporal rejects it, DBOS/Prefect are looser) per the maintainers' own open issue #5477
Kimi Agent SDK local-first status could not be determined even after a direct fetch - genuinely UNKNOWN, not inferred

Qwen-Agent documents a first-party local model execution path: vLLM (GPU) and Ollama (CPU+GPU) self-hosted, alongside DashScope hosted option - the strongest local-first model-execution signal found across all researched ecosystems

Tencent Youtu-Agent is CLOUD_ONLY as configured by default despite being named a 'high-priority local-first reference' by the original research brief - the brief's own framing was not confirmed by direct evidence
LangGraph's Checkpointer is a backend-agnostic interface; in-memory and SQLite are first-class local options, not a degraded fallback behind Postgres/Mongo
claims.note: First draft of this claim was wrong (implied Postgres/Redis required); corrected after re-reading the interface directly.

claims.claim: LangGraph has no built-in checkpoint retention/archival policy (unbounded table growth) or state-schema migration mechanism - two open, currently-unsolved upstream issues (#1138, #536)
LangGraph core is MIT; langgraph-api (deployment server) is Elastic License 2.0 - a genuine license split within one framework
Mastra licensing has three tiers: framework (Apache-2.0), platform/Studio (commercially metered, self-hostable or hosted), Enterprise Edition (separate license) - not a simple two-way split
Mastra Workspace bundles filesystem/command-execution/search/skills as independently-configurable capabilities with per-tool approval gating (requireApproval, requireReadBeforeWrite)
claims.note: Strongest match across all ecosystems researched to LabLaunchPad's own planned adapters/tools boundary.

claims.claim: OpenHands' own docs state its LLM-based security analyzer is explicitly not a complete prompt-injection solution; execute_tool() bypasses conversation analyzers/confirmation entirely
Letta treats durable AgentState, Memory, Session, and Knowledge as distinct concepts, self-hosted via Docker/PostgreSQL
Google ADK's local/container execution exists but platform services (Agent Runtime/Cloud Run/GKE) materially expand the surface beyond a pure local core
Browser Use is a deliberately minimal, thin task+environment abstraction with a local OSS browser as the default execution path
CrewAI separates the open-source framework from the managed AMP platform explicitly
Strands Agents documents an Ollama provider for local invocation, streaming, and tool/function calling
smolagents defaults to local/HF/provider model support with agent memory local by default

AG2's license is split by code provenance: Apache-2.0 for fork modifications, MIT retained for original pre-fork AutoGen code - a third license-split variant distinct from LangGraph's by-directory and Mastra's by-tier splits
LlamaIndex core repository is MIT; individual integrations may vary in license - explicit variance flagged by the source itself
Llama Agents + Workflows local-first status is HYBRID, depending on selected model/deployment
Haystack documents HF local, llama.cpp, and Ollama model providers - the strongest local-model-provider breadth of batch 2; its own repository also flags an unreviewed license-header file

DSPy is architecturally a programming/optimization framework over an LM adapter (prompt/program compilation), not an agent runtime with tools/memory/workflow in the usual sense - a category difference from every other researched framework
Microsoft AutoGen is migration-era research; its documented successor is Microsoft Agent Framework
Microsoft Semantic Kernel is migration-era research; its documented successor is Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0, which explicitly supports Ollama

contradictions.topic: Whether a framework's root LICENSE file is sufficient due diligence
contradictions.claim_a: Installments 1-2's own methodology: fetch and quote the root LICENSE file, treat as the framework's licensing status
contradictions.claim_b: LangGraph (core MIT / langgraph-api Elastic 2.0), Mastra (framework Apache-2.0 / platform metered / Enterprise separate), and AG2 (Apache-2.0 for fork changes / MIT for pre-fork code) each split their license in a DIFFERENT way - by directory, by commercial tier, and by code provenance respectively
contradictions.resolution: claim_a is false as a general assumption, confirmed 3 separate ways across 8 directly-researched frameworks. Whole-tree/whole-offering checks are now a standing rule, not applied retroactively to the 5 frameworks researched under the old methodology (research/licensing/MATRIX.md's Whole tree checked? column is honestly "No" for those five).
contradictions.architecture_impact: MEDIUM - affects any future LabLaunchPad dependency-review process
contradictions.revisit_trigger: Formalizing a dependency-review gate for this repository.

contradictions.topic: Whether LangGraph requires PostgreSQL/Redis for local operation
contradictions.claim_a: First draft of this repository's own LangGraph research: "PostgreSQL + Redis are the documented requirement for durable, multi-process production use", verdict HYBRID
contradictions.claim_b: Direct re-reading of LangGraph's Checkpointer interface: in-memory and SQLite are first-class local options, not a degraded fallback; Postgres/Mongo are optional swappable backends
contradictions.resolution: claim_a conflated one deployment guide's production recommendation with a hard SDK requirement. Corrected to LOCAL_CAPABLE.
contradictions.architecture_impact: LOW - correction of this repository's own error, not an external contradiction

contradictions.topic: Whether side effects with ambiguous remote outcomes need a first-class UNKNOWN_OUTCOME state
contradictions.claim_a: Not addressed in this repository's Phase 0 architecture (no explicit UNKNOWN_OUTCOME concept in docs/architecture/PACKAGE-MAP.md as materialized)
contradictions.claim_b: 3 independently-supplied corpora (batch2's ADR-CANDIDATE-006; the post-commit-ops governance bundle's MERGE_UNKNOWN/DEPLOY_UNKNOWN/RECONCILING states; wave1's own concept file on scoped exactly-once semantics plus its E5-A durable-restart benchmark plan) all independently propose the same requirement
contradictions.resolution: Not a contradiction in the adversarial sense (nothing says UNKNOWN_OUTCOME modeling is wrong) - a convergence-strength finding: this is the single most corroborated architectural gap across all 6 corpora combined.
contradictions.architecture_impact: HIGH - directly informs the @lablaunchpad/state and @lablaunchpad/task package designs (Phase 3-4)
contradictions.revisit_trigger: When Phase 3/4 (core, task, state packages) design begins.

contradictions.topic: Whether workspace/sandbox needs to be an explicit, named architectural boundary
contradictions.claim_a: docs/architecture/PACKAGE-MAP.md's planned packages do not currently name a WorkspaceEngine or SandboxEngine boundary
contradictions.claim_b: 4 independent sources (OpenHands/Browser Use/Letta via batch1; Mastra's Workspace via this session's own live research; Youtu-Agent's Environment via this session's own live research; and the sandbox-execution topic's Docker/Firecracker/Wasmtime tradeoff analysis via batch3) all independently converge on workspace/sandbox as a first-class, explicit contract
contradictions.resolution: Not a contradiction - a genuine gap in the current package map, evidenced strongly enough to flag explicitly in ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md below.
contradictions.revisit_trigger: Phase 19 (SandboxProvider) design, or earlier if a WorkspaceEngine/SandboxEngine package is proposed before then.
